name: DDoS as a Smokescreen
definition: A distributed denial-of-service event functions as a diversion associated with another malicious operation, rather than availability loss alone accounting for the entire incident.
temporal_constraint: Contextually related overlap or continuity; timing alone is insufficient.
evidence_requirements: Corroboration of a functional relationship beyond temporal coincidence
Consider independent incidents and alternative explanations
exclusion_criteria: Unrelated concurrent incidents without corroborating linkage
defensive_significance: Maintain independent investigation of anomalous events during service disruption and avoid prematurely closing correlated incidents.

references.relevance: Recognizes distraction as a possible purpose of denial of service.
2018 academic description of DDoS as a Smokescreen; establishes prior terminology, not independent validation of this proposed schema.

strategic_property: Diversionary concealment: a disruptive activity functions to redirect defensive attention away from a separate malicious activity. This property is relational, not inherent to network flooding.

prior_art.distinction: ATT&CK maps the denial-of-service mechanism and acknowledges distraction; this candidate assigns a separate identifier to the functional relationship.
The term and detection problem predate SCCF. SCCF proposes a reusable classification record; it does not claim discovery of the attack.
Attack Flow describes connected activities; this entry proposes a named strategic relationship class. Exact overlap and interoperability require further review.
